subject: Post-demo: usage bands, budget guardrails & one-off credit authorization request
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha@brightpath.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 10:14:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps (tokens, budget bands, and credit ask)

Thanks again for making time today, Samantha — appreciated the level of detail on your internal latency targets and the two primary workloads (interactive assistant + nightly batch summarization). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock a small pilot that fits your procurement window:

1) Estimated monthly token profile (based on what we heard today):
   - Interactive assistant (peak): 8k–12k tokens/session, ~120 sessions/day => ~18–40M tokens/month
   - Nightly batch summarization: 250M tokens/month (within current ETL jobs)
   => Ballpark: 270–300M tokens/month; we should plan pricing and caching around 200–350M bands.

2) Budget range you indicated: ~$30k–$75k/month for initial phase (you said finance prefers a conservative band).

3) Unit economics target: you mentioned an internal target of ~$800–$1,200 per 1M tokens (net after any infra efficiencies). We should run a quick cost model to show projected $/1M across supported quantization levels.

4) Trial credits: based on the expected burn profile you outlined, I recommend a one-time pilot credit to cover ~50M tokens of the initial spike so your team can validate SLOs without hitting procurement blockers. If that sounds reasonable I can request approval from our pricing desk.

Next steps (proposed):
- Samantha: confirm whether procurement needs a PO before we can ship any credits and whether the budget band above maps to a committed term.
- BrightPath: share a short sample of anonymized inference logs (we only need shape + sequence lengths) — sample attached.
- Redwood: I’ll pull together a 3-band pricing model (200M / 275M / 350M) and a one-off credit ask for internal approval; loop in Lauren for the credit authorization.

Attached: redwood_pricing_bands_v2.xlsx (pricing bands draft), sample-inference-logs.jsonl (log shape, sanitized)

Thanks — I’m available for a quick 20-min follow-up Wed/Thu this week if that helps.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Samantha Lowe <samantha@brightpath.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (tokens, budget bands, and credit ask)

Hi Marcus — good summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement details: finance will need a PO for any billable activity, but they are comfortable with a one-off credit applied against the first invoice. We don’t need the PO to start a timeboxed pilot as long as the credit is documented in writing.

- Budget: the $30k–$75k band is accurate for Q1; Ops prefers we aim for the lower half (~$35k–$45k) initially and prove reduction levers (caching, selective quantization) before scaling.

- Unit economics: $800/1M is aggressive for our usage pattern — we expect somewhere closer to $1,000–$1,100/1M with conservative batching. If Redwood can show a path to $850/1M at 275M tokens with caching we’d be much more comfortable.

On the credits: we’d accept a one-time 50M token credit applied to the pilot. Please include the credit terms (expiry, usage restrictions) in the note to procurement.

I’ve attached an anonymized sample of three request traces — hope that helps. Can Neha confirm whether Redwood needs full KV-cache traces or just sequence-length and latency distributions?

Thanks — Sam
Samantha Lowe
Director of AI | BrightPath AI
samantha@brightpath.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha@brightpath.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (tokens, budget bands, and credit ask)

Appreciate the clarity, Sam. I’ll include a short credit memo for procurement that covers:
- Amount: 50M token credit applied to first invoice
- Expiry: 60 days from issuance
- Restriction: credit applies only to inference tokens (not embeddings or other billed items)

I’m looping in Lauren to sign off on the credit terms and accounting treatment. Neha, could you confirm the telemetry we need to run the caching/quantization model? If you can indicate whether sequence-length distributions alone would produce a reasonable estimate, we can avoid pulling KV cache content.

I’ll also attach the initial pricing bands spreadsheet to the procurement memo and push to HubSpot.

—Marcus
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Samantha Lowe <samantha@brightpath.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 13:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (tokens, budget bands, and credit ask)

Hi all — quick technical note from the SE side: sequence-length distributions + percentiles (P50/P95/P99) and a small sample of request/response token counts are sufficient for an initial cost projection and caching impact analysis. We don’t need KV caches or payload contents for the pricing exercise — sanitized logs are fine (what Marcus attached works).

Operational considerations:
- For the interactive assistant, enabling prefix caching for 60% of sessions (estimated) reduces token spend ~25% at P95.
- For nightly batch jobs, batching and tokenization pre-processing will be key; quantization to int8 for the summarization model is likely viable and gives ~30–40% cost reduction in production.

Lauren — for the one-off credit, can you confirm whether we route this through our standard promotional credits flow or handle as an administrative invoice adjustment? If standard promo, we’ll need the internal promo code and expiry; if invoice adjustment, procurement will need formal approval language.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
